![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14264628/assets/98d842c0c8af27575d5d31eb30679e4ae66f97e209c48107919f727c404366aa.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=-6+8x-2{x}^{2}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6+8x-2{x}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-4x+3 & =0 \\ (x-3)(x-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=1$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=1$ to $x=3.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}x(-6+8x-2{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}(-6x+8{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}(-3x+4{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
